bib.title: Foundations of Large Language Models, Chapter 1: Pre-training

read.skipped: none; the chapter PDF (35 pages) has no reference list, so citations were not checked against a bibliography

question: How is self-supervised pre-training done for decoder-only, encoder-only and encoder-decoder Transformers, and how is a pre-trained model (BERT as the example) adapted to downstream NLP tasks?
contributions: Taxonomy of self-supervised pre-training tasks by objective (Table 1.1)
BERT as a worked example: loss, setup, scaling, efficiency, multilingual variants
Recipes for adapting BERT to classification, regression, tagging, span prediction and encoder-decoder use

limits: Introductory; the text says it cannot cover all aspects of pre-training and defers large generative LLMs to later chapters
No experiments or new numbers; all figures are reported from BERT, RoBERTa, Megatron, XLM-R papers
Encoder-centric (BERT 2019 era); no coverage of scaling laws, data mixes, tokenizers, optimizers, LR schedules or training compute
No PDF version date printed; the PDF metadata is empty and the file has no reference list
practices: Use self-supervised pre-training and then adapt by fine-tuning or prompting (Sec 1.1)
When fine-tuning an encoder, either update all parameters or freeze the encoder and train only the classifier (Sec 1.1.2.1)
Keep a share of unchanged selected tokens in MLM to cut the [MASK] train/test mismatch (Sec 1.3.1.1)
Scale up on simple pre-training tasks with more data and compute; NSP can be dropped (Sec 1.3.2)
Mitigate catastrophic forgetting in fine-tuning by mixing in old data, experience replay or EWC (Sec 1.4)
Choose denoising corruption methods for encoder-decoder pre-training by careful experiment (Sec 1.2.3.2)
Use instruction-style prompts and few-shot demonstrations to adapt generative LLMs without training (Sec 1.1.2.2)

terms.definition: a neural network is trained using supervision signals derived from the data itself, rather than from human annotations
conventional language modeling, a special case of masked LM where right context is masked and each token is predicted from its left context
mask out some input tokens and train a model to predict them from all unmasked tokens, giving a bidirectional model
autoregressive prediction in an arbitrary factorization order, implemented with self-attention masks while the input order is unchanged
binary classification of whether SentB follows SentA, using the [CLS] output
a small generator MLM replaces tokens and a discriminator labels each token original or replaced
the encoder reads a prefix and the decoder predicts the rest causally
encoder receives a corrupted input and the decoder reconstructs the original
few-shot learning by adding demonstrations of input-output pairs to the prompt
MLM over packed parallel sentence pairs so that predicting a masked token can use the other language
a fixed-capacity model trained on too many languages suffers parameter competition and degrades on high-resource languages
switching among languages within a text
